title: Review: Forces and momentum
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Physics (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-29-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: A.2.13#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.2#c35 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; A.2#c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; A.2#c19 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: A.2#q19, A.2#q21, A.2#q24, A.2#q25, A.2#q26, A.2#q37, A.2#q20, A.2#q35, A.2#q22, A.2#q36, A.2#q27, A.2#q28. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: The scalar mv²/2, the total of which decreases when two bodies stick together on impact.

items.label: Angular velocity, ω
items.clue: The rate at which the angle swept out by the radius of a body in circular motion changes.

items.label: Force
items.clue: A push or pull that one body exerts on another as a result of an interaction between them.

items.label: Mass
items.clue: A measure of a body's inertia, its resistance to a change in velocity, and of the amount of matter it contains.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.060 kg moving at 30 m s⁻¹ strikes a wall at right angles and rebounds along the same line at 20 m s⁻¹. Taking the direction towards the wall as positive, what impulse does the wall exert on the ball?
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v − u) = 0.060 kg × (−20 − 30) m s⁻¹ = −3.0 N s: 3.0 N s directed away from the wall.

questions.stem: Sand falls vertically onto a horizontal conveyor belt at a steady rate of 0.80 kg s⁻¹. The belt moves at a constant 2.5 m s⁻¹, and the sand quickly reaches the speed of the belt. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal force that the belt exerts on the sand?
questions.explanation: The mass on the belt is changing, so F = Δp/Δt must be used. Each second, 0.80 kg of sand gains a horizontal velocity of 2.5 m s⁻¹: F = v(Δm/Δt) = 2.5 × 0.80 = 2.0 N.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.50 kg moving at 4.0 m s⁻¹ collides head-on with a stationary ball of mass 1.5 kg. After the collision, the 0.50 kg ball moves back along its original line at 2.0 m s⁻¹ and the 1.5 kg ball moves forwards at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which conclusion about the collision is correct?

options.text: It is elastic: the total kinetic energy is 4.0 J before and after.
It is impossible: the momentum after is 4.0 kg m s⁻¹, not 2.0.
It is inelastic, because the kinetic energy of the 0.50 kg ball decreased.
It is impossible, as the momentum of the 0.50 kg ball was not conserved.

questions.explanation: Momentum: before 0.50 × 4.0 = 2.0 kg m s⁻¹; after 0.50 × (−2.0) + 1.5 × 2.0 = 2.0 kg m s⁻¹, so the data are consistent. Kinetic energy: before ½ × 0.50 × 4.0² = 4.0 J; after 1.0 J + 3.0 J = 4.0 J. Total E_k is unchanged, so the collision is elastic.

questions.stem: Two ice skaters stand at rest facing each other on smooth ice. Skater A, of mass 60 kg, pushes skater B, of mass 45 kg, and they move apart in opposite directions along a straight line. Immediately afterwards B moves at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Friction is negligible. What is the speed of A?

options.text: 2.0 m s⁻¹
1.5 m s⁻¹
1.7 m s⁻¹
0.0 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: The total momentum is zero before the push, so it is zero after: 60 × v_A = 45 × 2.0, giving v_A = 1.5 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction to B.

questions.stem: A trolley of mass 0.50 kg moving at 6.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary trolley of mass 1.0 kg on a straight, frictionless track. The trolleys stick together and move off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is transferred to other forms in the collision?
questions.explanation: E_k before = ½ × 0.50 × 6.0² = 9.0 J. E_k after = ½ × 1.5 × 2.0² = 3.0 J. Kinetic energy transferred to internal energy and sound = 9.0 − 3.0 = 6.0 J.

questions.stem: A body moves in uniform circular motion. Which single change would double its centripetal acceleration?

options.text: Doubling the speed while keeping the radius the same
Doubling the radius, with the speed unchanged
Halving the radius while keeping the speed the same
Halving the time period, with the radius unchanged

questions.explanation: a = v²/r, so at a fixed speed the acceleration is inversely proportional to the radius: halving r doubles a. A tighter circle at the same speed needs a larger inward acceleration.

questions.stem: Two identical eggs are dropped from the same height. One lands on a thick foam cushion and stops without breaking; the other lands on a concrete floor, stops and breaks. Neither egg bounces. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Each egg receives the same impulse, but the foam acts for longer, so the average force is smaller.
The foam reduces the egg's change in momentum, so the average force exerted on it is smaller.
The foam absorbs the force of the falling egg, so less force is left to act on the egg's shell.
The foam absorbs the egg's kinetic energy, so unlike the concrete it exerts no force on the egg.

questions.stem: A rocket travels through deep space, far from any star or planet. Its engine ejects exhaust gas backwards at a constant rate and at a constant speed relative to the rocket. Which statement about the acceleration of the rocket while the engine is firing is correct?

options.text: It stays constant, because a constant thrust produces a constant acceleration.
It is zero, because there is nothing in empty space for the exhaust gas to push against.
It decreases, because the force that the engine gives the rocket is gradually used up.
It increases, because the mass of the rocket keeps decreasing as fuel is used up.

questions.stem: Which statement describes an elastic collision between two bodies?

options.text: The bodies bounce apart after colliding, instead of sticking together.
The total kinetic energy of the two bodies is the same before and after.
At least one of the bodies is made of a stretchy material such as rubber.
Momentum is conserved, which is not the case in an inelastic collision.

questions.explanation: An elastic collision is defined by the conservation of total kinetic energy. Total momentum is conserved too, as it is in every collision of an isolated system.

questions.stem: A body at rest on a smooth horizontal surface explodes into two pieces, of masses m and 3m, which move apart along a straight line. External forces are negligible during the explosion. Which statement about the pieces immediately after the explosion is correct?

options.text: The two pieces move apart with equal speeds, as the forces on them were equal.
The lighter piece moves away three times as fast as the heavier piece does.
The two pieces carry equal kinetic energies, as the energy is shared out equally.
The total momentum of the pieces is greater than that of the body beforehand.

questions.stem: A firework shell is at rest when it explodes into several fragments. External forces can be ignored during the explosion. Which statement about the fragments immediately after the explosion is correct?

options.text: Their total momentum has increased, as has their total kinetic energy.
Their total momentum is zero, and so is their total kinetic energy.
Their total momentum is zero and their total kinetic energy has increased.
Their total momentum is zero, and the total energy of the system has risen.

questions.explanation: The explosive forces are internal, so the total momentum stays zero: the fragments' momenta cancel as vectors. Chemical energy is transferred to kinetic energy, so the total kinetic energy, zero before, has increased.

questions.stem: The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?
questions.explanation: r = 0.25 m. a = 4π²r/T² = 4π² × 0.25/(0.050)² = 3.9 × 10³ m s⁻², directed towards the axis of the drum.
